newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 25.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on March 25. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Indonesian rescuers have discovered the body of geologist Michael de Guzman who fell to his death from a helicopter which took him to the Busang gold find. Gusman, a Filipino national who has helped discover the find, was found dead on Sunday in a swamp.

Secretary-general of the Ministry of Tourism, Post and Telecommunications Jonathan Parapak has reiterated that state-owned telecommunication company PT Telkom would keep its exclusive rights to provide long-distance calls until 2006 and domestic calls until 2011.

The government still allows new foreign investments in oil palm plantantions in eastern Indonesia. But foreign investors will be required to involve smallholders in their plantation projects under the nucleus and smallholder scheme to ensure locals benefited directly from foreign investment.
Standby loans worth $500 million will be signed today between Indonesia's central bank, Bank Indonesia, and 40 foreign banks from Asia, Australia and the United States.

The government is being urged to set up an independent team to probe a reported manipulation of data by Bre-X Minerals Ltd on the Busang mine's gold reserves. The stocks of Canada's Bre-X took a tumble on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Friday following reports the gold find was not as big as the 70.9 million ounces first thought.
